subject: Planned unpin window & staged recovery ladder — FinovateBank private fleet
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finovatebank.com>, Michael Sweeney <michael.sweeney@cloudops-partners.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Version pin unfreeze proposal & contingency ladder — FinovateBank private fleet

Team, Priya, Michael —

Quick note to start a short planning thread for the targeted "unpin" window we discussed for FinovateBank's private deployment. This is scoped to the active VPC fleet running 2027.09.x (pinned) and the proposed plan is to unpin to 2027.11.1 for a week of staged rollout so we can validate kernel and quant optimizations.

Key constraints / asks from our side:
- Non-disruptive warmup: no full-evictions unless we hit hard failure triggers.
- Visible triggers: we want to capture error-rate, 95/99 latency shifts, KV cache miss ratio, and a per-model degraded-quality signal.
- Grace periods: an eviction window should have a short grace to allow in-flight requests to finish where feasible.

Proposal (draft):
- Maintenance window: Sunday 2027-11-28 01:00–05:00 UTC for initial unpin staging (canary 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% across two nights).
- Monitoring gates: automatic rollback / shelving if sustained error-rate > 3% over 15m or 95th latency increases > 40% versus baseline for the canary group.
- Eviction policy: 10-minute grace period before forced eviction per pod, with an escalating stall-mitigation ladder if progress stalls.

I've attached a lightweight triggers spec (unpin-triggers.yaml) and a human-readable guidelines doc (staged-eviction-guidelines.md). Please review and call out any customer constraints we need to surface (maintenance blackout windows, audit requirements, etc.).

Next step: if Priya confirms the dates are acceptable we will open the JIRA runbook and schedule the preflight call.

Thanks,

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Attachments: unpin-triggers.yaml (text), staged-eviction-guidelines.md (text)

Subject: Re: Version pin unfreeze proposal & contingency ladder — FinovateBank private fleet

Thanks Soojin — a few clarifications from our side before we confirm dates:

1) Grace vs. forced eviction: can you explain what "10-minute grace" means in practice for long-running streaming sessions? Our customers will see spiky errors if we interrupt in-flight sessions too aggressively.
2) Stall-mitigation ladder: we need explicit max pause durations we can tolerate (e.g., how long can you hold rolling pause before we need to abort and repin).
3) Audit evidence: we will need the runbook and the post-upgrade telemetry snippets for our SOC audit (timestamps, who initiated, who approved).

Also, Wed night is a heavier traffic period for one of our east-coast partners — would you be open to moving the initial canary to Sunday midnight UTC instead of early Sunday morning?

— Priya
Priya Shah
Ops Lead, FinovateBank
priya.shah@finovatebank.com

Subject: Re: Version pin unfreeze proposal & contingency ladder — FinovateBank private fleet

Priya — good questions. Answers below and updated actions attached.

1) Grace for streaming: the 10-minute grace is a soft window where the node will stop accepting new prefixed sessions but will allow currently accepted streams up to 10m to finish. If a stream exceeds 10m and is still active, the node will move to a token-drain then a soft-shutdown; we only force-evict after an additional 5 minutes if progress stalls. We can label streaming endpoints to apply a longer grace if Finovate has premium flows that must survive (we should list those endpoints in the runbook).

2) Stall-mitigation ladder (conservative defaults):
- Tier 1: Pause canary rollout up to 30 minutes for investigation (auto-notify).
- Tier 2: Extend pause up to 2 hours if mitigation steps are in progress (manual approval required from Finovate Ops + Redwood oncall).
- Tier 3: Repin & rollback if no safe lift within 2 hours or sustained error-rate > 5% for 30m.

3) Audit evidence: we will write the runbook section that records who clicked the "unpin" action, timestamps, pre/post telemetry snapshots and attach to the postmortem. Draft runbook link and JIRA ticket included below.

Schedule note: moving to Sunday 2027-11-28 00:00–04:00 UTC (initial canary night) works for us; Monica will own preflight checks and Michael (CloudOps partner) will coordinate network cordon.

Attached: rollback-checklist.pdf (play-by-play), updated triggers spec.

Thanks,

— Monica
Monica Patel
Senior SRE, Private Ops — Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

Attachments: rollback-checklist.pdf (pdf)

Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 07:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Version pin unfreeze proposal & contingency ladder — FinovateBank private fleet

Thanks for the rapid feedback. Two additional asks from product/SLT before we lock the window:

- Explicit grace eviction definition: we will set the default to 10m soft-grace + 5m forced-evict. For labeled premium streams we will allow 30m soft-grace + 10m forced-evict. Please confirm the list of premium endpoints by Thursday EOD.

- Stalled-upgrade mitigation (new): when a canary group stalls (no progress in pod warmup for > 12m), we will attempt an immediate cache-warm restart on the canary group once (non-destructive) and then pause for human triage. If the restart fails or restarts exceed 3 attempts within 1 hour, we will shelf the entire canary and repin.

Operational asks for Finovate: can you confirm whether you can tolerate a rolling pause of up to 2 hours during the staged rollout (we'll only use the full 2hr when human triage is required). If not, please state a max tolerable pause.

I'll schedule a 30-minute preflight on Friday to review playbook roles (Monica = owner, Soojin = approval, Rishi = exec escalation).

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Product — Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Thanks Rishi — we can accept the defaults with two caveats:
1) For any premium stream requiring >10m grace, Finovate will provide an allowlist of endpoints by Thursday EOD and reserve the right to pause the rollout for business-hours traffic concerns.
2) If the shelf/repin path is exercised, Finovate requests a post-action telemetry snapshot and a joint incident review within 48 hours (we need this for audit).

Action items confirmed:
- Monica: preflight checklist and runbook owner (Monica to attach final checklist to JIRA).
- Soojin: finalize triggers spec and upload to shared Drive (link requested).
- Rishi: schedule preflight and create JIRA OPS-4521 runbook ticket.

We'll be on the preflight call Friday 09:00 UTC.

— Priya

Subject: Final: Unpin window confirmed + owner/action summary — FinovateBank

Summary and owners per today's confirmations: 

1) Window: Sunday 2027-11-28 00:00–04:00 UTC (initial canary night). Monica will execute the staged rollout (10%->30%->60%->100%).

2) Grace & eviction: default 10m soft-grace + 5m forced-evict; premium endpoints 30m + 10m. Finovate to provide allowlist by 2027-12-02 EOD.

3) Stall mitigation: on >12m no-progress we attempt one cache-warm restart (non-destructive). If restarts fail (>=3 attempts in 1 hour) we shelf canary and repin.

4) Pause tolerance: Finovate confirmed up to 2 hours pause for human triage.

5) Audit artifacts: Monica to attach final rollback-checklist.pdf to JIRA OPS-4521; Soojin to upload runbook to Drive and tag Finovate for SOC evidence. Rishi will create the postmortem template for the joint review.

Links & tickets: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/finovate-unpin-runbook , JIRA-OPS-4521

If there are no objections I will lock the window and send calendar invites for the preflight and the 30-minute runbook walk-through.

Thanks everyone —

— Rishi
